guidelines: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 189: Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy
assessment: Nausea and vomiting affect up to 80% of pregnant individuals in the 1st trimester, typically driven by rising beta-hCG and estrogen concentrations, peaking around weeks 8-10.
lifestyleMeasures: Eat small, frequent protein-rich and complex carbohydrate meals every 1-2 hours to prevent an empty stomach.
Keep dry crackers or plain toast at the bedside and eat before rising.
Ginger supplements (250 mg four times daily) or ginger tea show clinical efficacy in mild nausea.
Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine 10-25 mg three times daily) is considered first-line safe pharmacological therapy under obstetric supervision.
redFlags: Inability to keep liquids down for >24 hours, dark concentrated urine, dizziness on standing, or weight loss >5% of pre-pregnancy weight indicates Hyperemesis Gravidarum requiring IV rehydration and hospital review.

guidelines: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia
assessment: Preeclampsia is a multisystem disorder characterized by new-onset hypertension (systolic >= 140 mmHg or diastolic >= 90 mmHg on two occasions) after 20 weeks of gestation, often with proteinuria or organ dysfunction.
warningSymptoms: Persistent frontal headache non-responsive to acetaminophen
Visual disturbances (scotoma, blurred vision, flashing spots)
Right upper quadrant / epigastric abdominal pain
Sudden rapid edema of the face, hands, or periorbital area
redFlags: Any BP >= 160/110 mmHg or severe persistent epigastric pain is a critical hypertensive emergency. Proceed to the labor & delivery emergency room immediately or call 112.
